hearing.caseNumberRestrictions: Only hearing date criteria apply to case-number hearing search.

semantics: Unknown and mode-incompatible fields fail before navigation; first/last name are both required.
Asterisk wildcard requires at least two leading characters; wildcard and Sounds Like cannot be combined.
Dates use valid ISO YYYY-MM-DD at the boundary, converted to the observed control's native format. A single date selects On; two differing dates select Range.
Case identity must match the requested nonempty case number; re-acquired document identity must be unique, never ordinal.
Every observed ROA content section retains source label and sanitized text; non-document events and multiple attachments are retained.
Hidden form tokens remain ephemeral for acquisition and are removed from persisted observations.
The 200-result cap or an unconsumed next page makes discovery incomplete. No universal statewide coverage claim.
Name-based searches do not expose pending criminal matters; absence is not proof of nonexistence.
Document index numbers may exist without attachments. Restricted public-record availability is not a download failure to bypass.
Visible CAPTCHA/challenge blocks stop acquisition. Standard Playwright only; no stealth plugin, proxies, or identity cycling.

Isolated BrowserContext routing budgets every source-origin document, XHR and fetch request, including the initial request of a popup. Stylesheets, fonts and images are excluded. Missing interception support fails explicitly; HTTP 403/429 latches a block, including requests awaiting a budget, and preserves Retry-After.

Legacy CLI uses the configured minimum request interval without a database callback. Standalone and extension paths create owned contexts with serviceWorkers blocked. Extension isolation is attempted through its CDP Browser.newContext API; actual unsupported failures are explicit and never fall back to the operator's shared context.
Result-readiness timeouts inspect visible CAPTCHA/challenge state before propagating the original timeout; HTTP-200 challenge pages become blocked rather than retryable timeouts.
Legacy search CLI uses canonical query validation, including --attorney-first/--attorney-middle and --search-type document|judgment|hearing. Proxy flags and proxy-test have been removed.

Legacy statewide requires --query JSON containing a validated source criterion. Filter-only enumeration is rejected before opening a browser; narrowed partition completeness is not statewide record coverage.
